subject: Shadow vs Bench: trial evaluation strategy and acceptance gates
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia Barnes <olivia@mediastream.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 3 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call recap + proposed POC evaluation approach (shadow vs bench)

Hi Olivia — great conversation this morning. Quick recap and suggested path for the POC so we can move to a scoped trial next week.

Summary of needs from your side:
- Conversational assistant for customer support triage (multi-turn).
- Hard constraint: PHI can appear in examples; PII redaction pipeline required.
- Throughput target: peak 120 rps, p95 latency < 350ms for golden flows.
- Success criteria: correctness of triage intent + safe (low hallucination).

High-level POC options (two complimentary tracks):
1) Offline benchmark (bench) — dataset-based evaluation:
   - Redwood runs batch evals against a labeled holdout of ~1,200 queries you provide + synthetic edge cases we generate.
   - Metrics: Top-1 intent accuracy, slot extraction F1, hallucination rate (manual label), answer safety score.
   - Acceptance gate (proposal): Top-1 >= 92%, slot F1 >= 88%, hallucination <= 3%.

2) Online shadow (shadow) — production-mirroring:
   - Route live traffic copies to Redwood in shadow mode for 2 weeks (no customer-facing changes).
   - Measure latency distribution, cache hit rate, and live disagreement rate against your current system.
   - Collect human review samples for live edge-cases and safety checks.

Why run both: bench lets us tune model/config quickly and establishes a labeled baseline. Shadow proves the model under real traffic characteristics (latency, concurrency, distribution shift).

Draft timeline (we can compress):
- Week 0 (this week): finalize scope, dataset access, and legal (NDA/KMS alignment).
- Week 1: Redwood prepares offline eval & baseline runs; Mediastream provides 1,200 labeled examples and access to sample live traffic stream for shadow provisioning.
- Week 2: Shadow run + ongoing annotations; internal weekly sync.
- Week 3: Collate results, apply remediation (model or prompt adjustments), run final acceptance bench.

Ownership suggestion:
- Redwood: run offline bench, provision shadow infra, produce evaluation reports and suggested model config. (Owner: Stephanie)
- Mediastream: provide labeled dataset, enable sample traffic mirror, and supply initial acceptance labelers or budget for Redwood-assisted labeling. (Owner: Olivia)

Open questions for you:
- Can you share the labeled examples by Friday? Prefer CSV with columns: uttrance,id,expected_intent,slots,redaction_flag.
- Do you have existing human reviewers we should route sampled disagreements to, or should Redwood provide labeling support?

Attachments: evaluation_rubric_v1.csv (initial scoring weights)

If this looks good I’ll schedule a 30-min alignment on Friday to lock the dataset access and labeling plan — proposed: Fri 11/6 10:00am PT.

Thanks — Stephanie

--
Stephanie Nguyen

Couple of pragmatic adjustments to propose and I attached an amended rubric sheet with weights.

Proposed scoring weights (amendment):
- Intent Accuracy (top-1): 40%
- Slot Extraction (F1): 25%
- Hallucination / Safety (manual): 20%
- Latency (p95 normalized): 10%
- Escalation Rate (false negative for urgent intents): 5%

Rationale: intent accuracy drives business outcomes so it should be the largest weight. Safety (hallucination) is critical given PHI exposure so keep that high. Latency is measured only in shadow and normalized vs your baseline (we'll provide p50/p95/p99).

Labeling guidelines (short):
- If intent is ambiguous, labelers should pick the most conservative intent (i.e., escalate) and mark "ambiguous" flag.
- For partial matches on slots, compute slot-level precision/recall; if key slots are missing (customer id, claim id), mark as critical failure.
- Hallucination: any system-generated assertion that contradicts source data or invents facts = hallucination.

Ownership & tooling:
- Redwood will deliver a live scoreboard and per-batch CSV with disagreement samples.
- Marissa: can you confirm whether Mediastream wants reviewer links as annotated Google Sheets or in our labeling UI?

[Attachment: evaluation_rubric_v1.csv (updated, 21KB)]

-Karthik
